idiom_name: hand-written route table over the decoded discriminator (kind string -> handler function pointer)
implementation_notes: C has no reflection, no dynamic dispatch and no messaging runtime, so the router is a data structure the developer writes: extract the routing field from the decoded frame into a bounded buffer, then walk a static table of key-to-handler rows and call the matching handler - the table, not the individual call sites, is the routing rules artifact. Keep the keys owned and length-checked before strcmp, and put the unroutable handler in the loop's fall-through so 'no match' is a visible code path instead of a silent drop; a vtable-based router structure is only justified when rules must be loaded at runtime. Over a broker the same shape appears as a client-side table keyed by topic or routing key, with the payload inspected after decode.
pitfalls: strcmp returns 0 when the strings are equal, so writing `if (strcmp(kind, route.kind))` inverts the decision and sends everything to the wrong branch (or straight to the fallback).
msg->kind arrives off the wire: if it is not guaranteed NUL-terminated, strcmp reads past the frame (undefined behaviour), so copy into a bounded buffer or compare a fixed width with memcmp first.

The table and the producer's kinds are two separate contracts: a new kind with no row silently reaches the unroutable handler, so alert on fallback volume instead of trusting that the table is complete.
